flagged.evidence: The title says “Group-like and primitive elements of a coalgebra,” but the Definition specifies that x is “primitive relative to g” for a specified group-like g, and notes that an arbitrary coalgebra has no distinguished unit. The title omits this essential qualification and suggests an ordinary primitive-element notion not defined here.

The title says “Group-like and primitive elements in a two-dimensional coalgebra,” while the Example states that the classified elements are “primitive relative to g” and that no multiplication or algebra unit is assumed. The result establishes only g-relative primitive elements, not ordinary primitive elements.

The Given clause assumes only a vector space, a comultiplication, and two maps satisfying the counit equations. Proof 2.1 nevertheless says “the associator and coassociativity identify its parenthesizations and maps.” The associator reparenthesizes tensor targets; equality of the iterated comultiplication maps requires coassociativity, which is not assumed. For instance, dualizing a unital nonassociative algebra with basis 1,a,b, products a²=b, ba=a, ab=bb=0, gives a counital but noncoassociative comultiplication.
